attack_mechanism: A fault on `openMSP430.cpu_en_s` can falsely complete an instruction or hold the execution machine in an earlier phase when `pc_nxt` is evaluated. Instruction fetch is released from `I_DEC` only when `exec_done` or `E_IDLE` is observed, and `e_state` also determines whether jump, source-write, or destination-write completion is pending. `openMSP430.cpu_en_s` controls that execution sequencing before the frontend selects the next PC update; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. Signal propagation follows `openMSP430.cpu_en_s -> openMSP430.frontend_0.cpu_halt_req -> openMSP430.frontend_0.fetch -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. The PC is advanced too early, held too long, or updated with operands belonging to the wrong instruction phase.

A transient bit flip or forced value on `openMSP430.cpu_en_s` before the next `mclk` edge can substitute a false target or assert the software-write selection on the wrong instruction. During a CALL, jump, or instruction that writes R0, `pc_sw_wr` has priority in the `pc_nxt` multiplexer and selects `pc_sw`. `openMSP430.cpu_en_s` participates in forming or qualifying that software-PC path; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.pc_sw_wr`. Signal propagation follows `openMSP430.cpu_en_s -> openMSP430.frontend_0.cpu_halt_req -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.exec_cycle -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. The corrupted target is captured in `pc`, redirecting control flow, skipping intended instructions, or executing an unintended basic block.

Instruction fetch is released from `I_DEC` only when `exec_done` or `E_IDLE` is observed, and `e_state` also determines whether jump, source-write, or destination-write completion is pending. `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_type_nxt` controls that execution sequencing before the frontend selects the next PC update; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.frontend_0.irq_detect`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. Signal propagation follows `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_type_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_so_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.fetch -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. The PC is advanced too early, held too long, or updated with operands belonging to the wrong instruction phase.

A transient bit flip or forced value on `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_type_nxt` before the next `mclk` edge can substitute a false target or assert the software-write selection on the wrong instruction. During a CALL, jump, or instruction that writes R0, `pc_sw_wr` has priority in the `pc_nxt` multiplexer and selects `pc_sw`. `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_type_nxt` participates in forming or qualifying that software-PC path; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_type_nxt`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.dst_acalc`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.pc_sw_wr`. Signal propagation follows `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_type_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_ad_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. The corrupted target is captured in `pc`, redirecting control flow, skipping intended instructions, or executing an unintended basic block.

Injecting a transient or stuck fault into `openMSP430.frontend_0.sconst_nxt` before `pc` is enabled can add the wrong increment or prevent the expected increment. With no software PC write and no interrupt-vector state active, `pc_nxt` falls through to `pc_incr = pc + {14'h0, fetch, 1'b0}`. `openMSP430.frontend_0.sconst_nxt` affects `fetch`, instruction length, or the instruction-state decision used by this sequential increment; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.dbg_halt_st`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.dst_inst_sext_sel`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. Signal propagation follows `openMSP430.frontend_0.sconst_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_sext -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add_inc -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. The next instruction is skipped, repeated, or fetched from an unintended address.

During a CALL, jump, or instruction that writes R0, `pc_sw_wr` has priority in the `pc_nxt` multiplexer and selects `pc_sw`. `openMSP430.inst_type` participates in forming or qualifying that software-PC path; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.frontend_0.cpu_halt_st`, `openMSP430.inst_type`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.pc_sw_wr`.
